title: Binary clock is not displayed in the panel under certain panel thicknesses
line: The Binary Clock now shows its dots in thin horizontal panels instead of an empty space, and bigger dots in thicker ones.
explanation: In a horizontal panel the applet asks for a width of (height - 5*smallSpacing)*dots/4, which only fits the dots, but dotSize then also subtracts (dots+1)*smallSpacing from that width. The width side therefore always wins and drops to 0 or less once the panel is thinner than about 50 px, so nothing is drawn (and even at 60 px the dots were 1 px). The change adds the spacing to the requested width, and uses a spacing that scales down with the height (at most smallSpacing, also used by the grid) so very thin panels still have room for dots.

commits.message:
applets/binary-clock: Keep the dots visible in thin panels

The applet asked for a width that only fit the dots, while dotSize also
subtracts the spacing from it, so in thinner panels the dots shrank to
nothing. Reserve that spacing too and scale it down in thin panels.

BUG: 482291

From 439d2364879fd07717e6094ac8e52a6b451bcfc3 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: =?UTF-8?q?Niccol=C3=B2=20Venerandi?= <niccolo@venerandi.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 16:39:04 +0100
Subject: [PATCH] applets/binary-clock: Keep the dots visible in thin panels

The applet asked for a width that only fit the dots, while dotSize also
subtracts the spacing from it, so in thinner panels the dots shrank to
nothing. Reserve that spacing too and scale it down in thin panels.

BUG: 482291
---
 applets/binary-clock/BinaryClock.qml | 8 ++++++--
 1 file changed, 6 insertions(+), 2 deletions(-)

diff --git a/applets/binary-clock/BinaryClock.qml b/applets/binary-clock/BinaryClock.qml
index 29e89342d..2ec12655f 100644
--- a/applets/binary-clock/BinaryClock.qml
+++ b/applets/binary-clock/BinaryClock.qml
@@ -29,7 +29,9 @@ import org.kde.plasma.plasmoid
 Item {
     id: main
 
-    readonly property real w1: (main.height-5*Kirigami.Units.smallSpacing)*dots/4
+    readonly property real spacing: Math.min(Kirigami.Units.smallSpacing, main.height/9)
+
+    readonly property real w1: (main.height-5*spacing)*dots/4 + (dots+1)*spacing
 
     Layout.minimumWidth: w1 < 20 ? 20 : w1
     Layout.maximumWidth: Infinity
@@ -56,7 +58,7 @@ Item {
     readonly property color onColor: Plasmoid.configuration.useCustomColorForActive ? Plasmoid.configuration.customColorForActive : Kirigami.Theme.textColor
     readonly property color offColor: Plasmoid.configuration.useCustomColorForInactive ? Plasmoid.configuration.customColorForInactive : Qt.rgba(onColor.r, onColor.g, onColor.b, 0.2)
 
-    readonly property int dotSize: Math.min((height-5*Kirigami.Units.smallSpacing)/4, (width-(dots+1)*Kirigami.Units.smallSpacing)/dots)
+    readonly property int dotSize: Math.min((height-5*spacing)/4, (width-(dots+1)*spacing)/dots)
 
     readonly property alias mouseArea: mouseArea
 
@@ -70,6 +72,8 @@ Item {
         anchors.horizontalCenter: parent.horizontalCenter
         anchors.verticalCenter: parent.verticalCenter
         columns: Plasmoid.configuration.showSeconds ? 6 : 4
+        rowSpacing: main.spacing
+        columnSpacing: main.spacing
         Repeater {
             model: [8, 4, 2, 1]
             Repeater {
--

media.caption: Default 46 px panel: the Binary Clock is an empty space at the right end
Default 46 px panel: the dots are shown
36 px panel: small but visible dots
60 px panel: dots sized to the panel height

review.text: Solid, minimal QML fix that accounts for inter-dot spacing in w1, scales spacing down proportionally in thin horizontal panels, and aligns GridLayout's rowSpacing/columnSpacing with the spacing used in dotSize. The math avoids negative sizes, overflow, and binding loops across thin, default, and thick panels as well as desktop placement, and the screenshots verify 36 px, 46 px, and 60 px panels convincingly. Leaving vertical-panel layout as a separate pre-existing issue is reasonable and honestly documented.

reviews.text: Solid, minimal QML fix that accounts for inter-dot spacing in w1, scales spacing down proportionally in thin horizontal panels, and aligns GridLayout's rowSpacing/columnSpacing with the spacing used in dotSize. The math avoids negative sizes, overflow, and binding loops across thin, default, and thick panels as well as desktop placement, and the screenshots verify 36 px, 46 px, and 60 px panels convincingly. Leaving vertical-panel layout as a separate pre-existing issue is reasonable and honestly documented.

The width formula fix is correct, and the spacing that scales with height makes the dots visible at 36, 46 and 60 px in horizontal panels, as the screenshots show; the cause and layer are right. The verify notes say the clock still draws nothing in a vertical panel, before and after the fix. That is the same symptom ('not displayed in the panel'), and the title isn't limited to horizontal panels, so BUG: 482291 would close the report while the widget stays invisible in vertical panels. The desktop spacing also changes slightly (from GridLayout's default 5 px to 4 px); that change is harmless.
changes: Handle the vertical form factor too (size the dots and the requested height from the panel width when Plasmoid.formFactor is Vertical), and show before/after media of a vertical panel.
If vertical panels are left for later, use CCBUG instead of BUG and say so; as it stands, the commit closes a bug it only fixes for horizontal panels.
